author: श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्य
commentary:
श्रीमदानन्दतीर्थभगवत्पादाचार्यविरचितम्
श्रीमद्भगवद्गीताभाष्यम् देवं नारायणं नत्वा सर्वदोषविवर्जितम् ।
परिपूर्णं गुरूंश्चाऽन् गीतार्थं वक्ष्यामि लेशतः ॥ नष्टधर्मज्ञानलोककृपालुभिर्ब्रह्मरुद्रेन्द्रादिभिरर्थितो ज्ञानप्रदर्शनाय भगवान् व्यासोऽवततार । ततश्चेष्टानिष्टप्राप्तिपरिहारसाधनादर्शनाद् वेदार्थाज्ञानाच्च संसारे क्लिश्यमानानां वेदानधिकारिणां स्त्रीशूद्रादीनां च धर्मज्ञानद्वारा मोक्षो भवेदिति कृपालुः सर्ववेदार्थोपबृंहितां तदनुक्तकेवलेश्वरज्ञानदृष्टार्थयुक्तां च सर्वप्राणिनाम् अवगाह्यानवगाह्यरूपां केवलभगवत्स्वरूपपरां परोक्षार्थां महाभारतसंहिताम् अचीक्लृपत् ॥ तच्चोक्तम् -
'लोकेशा ब्रह्मरुद्राद्याः संसारे क्लेशिनं जनम् ।
वेदार्थाज्ञमधीकारवर्जितं च स्त्रियादिकम् ॥
अवेक्ष्य प्रार्थयामासुर्देवेशं पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् व्यासो भूत्वा च तेन च ॥
अन्यावताररूपैश्च वेदानुक्तार्थभूषितम् ।
केवलेनात्मबोधेन दृष्टं वेदार्थसंयुतम् ॥
वेदादपि परं चक्रे पञ्चमं वेदमुत्तमम् ।
भारतं पञ्चरात्रं च मूलरामायणं तथा ॥
पुराणं भागवतं चेति सम्भिन्नः शास्त्रपुङ्गवः॥’ इति नारायणाष्टाक्षरकल्पे । ‘ब्रह्माऽपि तन्न जानाति ईषत् सर्वोऽपि जानति(ते)।
बह्वर्थमृषयस्तत्तु भारतं प्रवदन्ति हि ॥’ इत्युपनारदीये। ‘ब्रह्माद्यैः प्रार्थितो विष्णुर्भारतं स चकार ह ।
यस्मिन् दशार्थाः सर्वत्र न ज्ञेयाः सर्वजन्तुभिः ॥’ इति नारदीये । 'वेदाः सर्वे परा वेदाः भारतं परमेऽवस्थितम् ।
भारतं चापि कृतवान् पञ्चमं वेदमुत्तमम् ।
दशावरार्थं सर्वत्र केवलं विष्णुबोधकम् ॥
परोक्षार्थं तु सर्वत्र वेदादप्युत्तमं तु यत् ॥’ इति स्कान्दे । ‘यदि विद्याच्चतुर्वेदान् साङ्गोपनिषदान् द्विजः ।
न चेत् पुराणं संविद्यान्नैव स स्याद् विचक्षणः ॥’ (म.भा.१.१.२६८) ‘इतिहासपुराणाभ्यां वेदं समुपबृंहयेत् ।
‘बिभेत्यल्पश्रुताद् वेदो मामयं प्रचलिष्यति ।’ ( म.भा.आदि.१.२९३) मन्वादि केचिद् ब्रुवते ह्यास्तीकादि तथाऽपरे ।
तथोपरिचराद्यन्ये भारतं परिचक्षते ॥ (म.भा.आदि.१.६६) भारतं सर्ववेदाश्च तुलामारोपिताः पुरा ।
देवैर्ब्रह्मादिभिः सर्वैः ऋषिभिश्च समन्वितैः ।
व्यासस्यैवाज्ञया तत्र त्वत्यरिच्यत भारतम् ॥ (ब्रह्माण्डपुराणे) ‘महत्त्वाद् भारवत्त्वाच्च महाभारतमुच्यते ।
निरुक्तमस्य यो वेद सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते ॥’ (म.भा.१.३००) ‘यदिहास्ति तदन्यत्र यन्नेहास्ति न कुत्रचित् ’ ( म.भा.आदि ५.५०), ‘विराटोद्योगसारवान्’ ( म भा.१.८९) इत्यादितद्वाक्यपर्यालोचनया, ऋषिसम्प्रदायात्, ‘को ह्यन्यः पुण्डरीकाक्षान्महाभारतकृद् भवेत्’ ( वायुप्रोक्तवचनम्) इत्यादिपुराणग्रन्थान्तरगतवाक्यान्यथानुपपत्त्या, नारदाध्ययनादिलिङ्गैश्चावसीयते । कथमन्यथा भारतनिरुक्तिज्ञानमात्रेण सर्वपापक्षयः ? प्रसिद्धश्च सोऽर्थः । कथं चान्यस्य न कर्तुं शक्यते? ग्रन्थान्तरगतत्वाच्च नाविद्यमानस्तुतिः । न च कर्तुरेव । इतरत्रापि साम्यात् । तत्र च सर्वभारतार्थसंग्रहां वासुदेवार्जुनसंवादरूपां भारतपारिजातमधुभूतां गीताम् उपनिबबन्ध । तच्चोक्तम्–
‘भारतं सर्वशास्त्रेषु भारते गीतिका वरा ।
विष्णोः सहस्रनामापि ज्ञेयं पाठ्यं च तद् द्वयम् ॥’ इति महाकौर्मे । ‘स हि धर्मः सुपर्याप्तो ब्रह्मणः पदवेदने।’(म.भा.१३.१६.१२.) इत्यादि च । तत्र सेनयोर्मध्ये बान्धवादिमोहजालसंवृतं विषीदन्तम् अर्जुनं भगवानुवाच ।
translation:
Shrimad-Bhagavad-Gita-Bhashyam
Authored by Shri Aanandateerth Bhagavatpada-Acharya. I bow to the Deva Narayana, who is devoid of all defects,
who is complete in all respect and is also my Guru, I concisely speak the meaning of Gita. When the Knowledge of Dharma was seen destryed, on the prayers from the compassionate deities - Brahma, Rudra, Indra etc., Bhagawan took the Vayasa-avataar to show the correct Knowledge. Thereafter, the compassionate Lord, desiring to show the means of removing the undesirable suffering that had befallen the worlds and also to show the knowledge of dharma, through which Moksha is obtained, for the benefit of even those who don't have eligibility to study the Vedas, such as women and sudra, He suitably prepared the Mahabharata-Samhita, which speak not just the essence embodid in the Vedas, but even the knowledge that are within the direct perception of the Ishwara; which is for all beings, where there are meanings that can be grasped or are ungraspable (based on the pramata's (प्रमाता) abilities); which indirectly describe only the Bhagawan's swaroopa. It is thus said in Narayana-ashtaakshara-kalpa -
Brahmā, Rudra, and the other deities, seeing that people were afflicted by the sufferings of worldly existence, ignorant of the meaning of the Vedas, and that women and other groups were devoid of eligibility for Vedic study, prayed to the Supreme Person, the Lord of the gods. Then the Bhagawan, pleased with their prayer, manifested Himself in the form of Vyāsa. Through this form and through other incarnations, He revealed the essential wisdom — even those that He has spoken of in other avataars, that hasn't been spoken in the Vedas, through direct perception and endowed with the true meaning of the Vedas — by composing the great “fifth Veda”, which is even superior to the Vedas; The Mahābhārata, the Pañcarātra, the Moola Rāmāyaṇa, the Bhāgavata Purāṇa - are most Supreme amongst Shastras in many ways. It is said in Upa-Narada-Purana
Even the Brihaspati (Brahmā) does not know it completely, other know the meaning partially (based on their eligibility). The Rishis speak that Bharata contains many layers of meaning. It is said in the Narada-Purana
Vishnu only composed the Bharata on the prayers of Brahma etc., in which there are 10s of meanings everywhere, that is not known to all beings. It is said in Skandha-Purana
Bharata was also composed (by Him), which is the great fifth Veda, there are 10s of meanings everywhere, only describing the knowledge about Vishnu, thus the indirect knowledge about the Lord, whatever is there be known, can be obtained from this great Veda. Mahabharata says (1.2.235)-
Even if a Dwija (twice born, who have the eligibility for the studies of the Vedas), has mastered the Vedas along with the Upanishadas, but doesn't know the Purana, he has not obtained the complete knowledge, he has not seen the knowledge. Mahabharata (1.2.204)
Using the Itihasa and Purana, the Vedas should be studied. The Vedas fear those of limited knowledge, who have thus not strengthened their understanding, that they will distort me. In the Brahmanda-Purana -
Learned speak of three different levels of meaning -
(1) Manavadi [The ten qualities beginning with devotion (bhakti)—namely bhakti (devotion), jñāna (knowledge), vairāgya (detachment), prajñā (discernment), medhā (intelligence), dhṛti (fortitude), sthiti (steadiness), yoga (spiritual discipline), prāṇa (vital energy), and bala (strength)—along with śravaṇa (listening), manana (reflection), śīla (character), vinaya (humility), and the Veda, are referred to as ‘Manu'.
The form of Dharma is Yudhiṣṭhira; the embodiment of the ten qualities beginning with devotion is Bhīmasena; the form of śravaṇa and manana is Arjuna; the embodiment of śīla (good conduct) is Nakula; the embodiment of vinaya (humility) is Sahadeva; and the embodiment of the Veda is Draupadī.
(2) Aastikaadi [When the intention is only to present (or expound) the Pāṇḍavas, then the Mahābhārata is called ‘Āstikādi.’]
(3) Upcharaadi [Uparicara: that in which something has its beginning and end is called Uparicarādi. He who moves above or pervades all beings is called Uparicara—that is Nārāyaṇa. When the intention of the Mahābhārata is to expound only such Nārāyaṇa, it is then called Uparicarādi.] For these three—Manvādi, Āstikādi, and Uparicarādi—there is scriptural authority in the 42nd chapter of the Ādiparva of the Mahābhārata. In Brahmanda-Purana -
In ancient times, by the command of Lord Vyāsa, Brahmā and the other deities and sages assembled and compared the Bhārata with all the Vedas, and they found the weight (significance) of the Bhārata to be greater. Mahabharata (1.1.209)
Because of its profound inner value and greatness, it is called the ‘Mahābhārata’. Those who understand it along with its vyutpatti—the deeper etymological meanings of its words—become freed from all sins. 'Whatever is found in Mahabharata, that is what is found elsewhere, whatever is not here, that is not found elsewhere.' (MB 18.5.35). 'The essence of this composition is in Virata and Udyoga Parva.' (MB 1.1.104)etc., sentences are discussed in the Rishis Sampradaya. 'Who else other than from Pundarikaaksha, that Mahabharata can be written.' (Padma-Puran 1.1.43-44, Vishnu Puran 3.4-5, MB 12.334.9) - from such statements in Puranas, from the Guru-Shishya parampara system its study and teaching practices, having been said so by Sage Narada and other Paramhansa, and its euology in the Puranas, we must understand that it is created by Lord Narayana Himself. How is it that, merely by understanding the Nirukti (etymological explanation) of the name Mahābhārata, the destruction of all sins becomes possible? It is said so; therefore the scripture Mahābhārata is considered the greatest of all scriptures. (If the knowledge of the Nirukti of the name Mahābhārata truly destroyed all sins, then one ought to become instantly liberated. Therefore, the phrase ‘destruction of all sins’ should be understood with some reservation. The meaning should be that the amount of sin destroyed by knowing this Nirukti is greater than that destroyed by other meritorious actions—not that literal immediate liberation occurs.) How can it be said that no one other than the Supreme could compose this scripture? For this, one must look at the inner substance contained in the text.(The Mahābhārata expounds subjects seen through divine knowledge. It is not merely a narrative; it contains profound metaphysical insight, the meaning of the Vedas, the path of devotion, philosophical inquiry into truth, and the attainment of the four aims of human life. Therefore, the Mahābhārata is the supreme scripture.) This is not stated merely to praise the author; it is equally praise of the inherent qualities of the Mahābhārata itself. Except for Nārāyaṇa Himself, no one else could have composed this work. Its very uniqueness proves this. If we simply say, ‘The Mahābhārata is great because Nārāyaṇa composed it,’ then other texts too would have to be considered great, since they were also composed by learned scholars. Therefore, authorship alone is not a sufficient reason. Only the combination of authorship + the intrinsic principles within the text + its purpose + its transformative impact establishes its supreme nature.” There inside it, in form of a dialog between Vasudeva and Arjuna, like the nector of the Bharata named Parijata flower, did the Lord composed the Gita. Thus it it said in Maha-Kaurma-Purana -
'Amongst the Shastra - the Bharata, and in the Bharata, the Gita is supreme. Vishnu-sahasra-nama also along with it, these two, should be studied and taught. That Dharma (the collective of truth, justice, non-violence, and the like) is in fact entirely sufficient as a means for attaining the grace of the Supreme Brahman (and thus to obtain liberation - mokṣa). There, when Arjuna, surrounded by the net of attachment for his relatives and kinsmen, became despondent (overcome with grief) while standing between the two armies, then Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa spoke to him.
